document.title: Osama bin Laden: A Case Study
document.authors: Sandia National Laboratories, U.S. Department of Energy (Dr. Gary W. Richter)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), 1998 Missile Strikes on Bin Laden May Have Backfired
document.note: [Unclassified] Nearly 400-page open-source examination of the emerging al-Qaeda threat, compiled in response to the 1998 embassy bombings. It focuses on weapons of mass destruction and summarizes the August 7 bombings, the August 20 retaliatory strikes and al-Qaeda's ambitions. It concludes the strikes did little to solve the bin Laden problem and may have done more harm than good, and that diplomatic options are likely the most effective strategy.

events.description: Bombings of U.S. embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam, which prompted this study.
Retaliatory US cruise missile strikes, judged to have done little to solve the bin Laden problem and possibly more harm than good.
African US embassy bombings, including Nairobi. The attackers did not get as close to either embassy as they sought, and most deaths were among Kenyans.
Data-gathering cut-off for the study, on or about the beginning of November 1999.
Truck bombings of US embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam attributed to al-Qa'ida
US cruise missile strikes in retaliation for the embassy bombings, hitting targets in Afghanistan and Sudan (Al Shifa)

Earliest date of reported bin Laden/al-Qa'ida interest in WMD
US General Accounting Office publishes report 'Combatting Terrorism: Observations on the Threat of Chemical and Biological Terrorism', quoted by the author.
US cruise missile strikes referenced as the basis of pros/cons analysis of using force, including targeting bin Laden; the document says the US failed to justify its actions to the world afterward.
GAO report 'Combatting Terrorism: Observations on the Threat of Chemical and Biological Terrorism' published.
Osama bin Laden born in Riyadh (other reports say 1956 or 1958).
Bin Laden traveled to Afghanistan to help the mujahideen fight the Soviets.
Bin Laden left Saudi Arabia and moved to Sudan.

Seven rockets fired at US and UN targets in Islamabad.

Khalfan Khamis Mohamed arrested at Cape Town airport and flown to New York
Sharif sent ISI chief Ziauddin to Kandahar to demand closure of terror camps
Sharif and Ziauddin traveled to Dubai for talks with UAE leaders
UN Security Council voted 15-0 for sanctions on Taliban unless bin Laden handed over
Sheehan met Taliban UN representative Abdul Hakeem Mujahid
Mujahid met Karl Inderfurth in Washington
Wakil Ahmad Muttawakil appointed Taliban Foreign Minister
Report that bin Laden offered in a letter to Omar to leave Afghanistan under two conditions
Taliban reportedly disarm Arab Afghan units and move camps from eastern Afghanistan to Kabul area
Three-day Lashkar-e-Tayyaba conference began at Muridke
Ahmed Salame Mabruk (Salameh) extradited from Tirana.
Hani al Sibai arrested by Scotland Yard.
US cruise missile attacks on training camps near Khost.
East African embassy bombings in Kenya and Tanzania.
Fazul letters warning of security compromise, found on Wadih el Hage's computer.
Fatwa calling on Muslims to kill US military personnel and civilians.
Bin Laden interview with Al Quds Al Arabi in a cave near Kandahar.
Fatwa by Imam al-Hudhayfi at Jumah prayer against US troops in Saudi Arabia.
Hafiz Shabir Ahmad killed in Kashmir.
Bin Laden Time interview on targeting Americans.
Bin Laden ABC interview.
Bin Laden gives ABC interview threatening Americans.
Late 1993 al-Qaeda effort to obtain enriched uranium approved by Salim.
CIA agent collects soil sample near Al Shifa containing EMPTA traces.
CIA issues first intelligence report on Al Shifa.
New CIA report on Sudan-bin Laden chemical weapons link.
State Department analysts respond skeptically to CIA report.
Small Group of presidential advisors meets Clinton with evidence on bin Laden WMD.
US cruise missile strikes on Al Shifa and Khost camps.
Mamdouh Mahmud Salim arrested in Bavaria.
Al-Hayat claims bin Laden acquired nuclear weapons from Central Asia.
Indictment against bin Laden alleges al-Qaeda–Iraq understanding.
Bin Laden reportedly met Iraqi ambassador to Turkey.
Al-Hayat quotes Mabrouk on bin Laden's WMD.
Bin Laden interview with ABC's John Miller saying acquiring such weapons is a religious duty.
Bin Laden interview with Time correspondent on acquiring weapons.
Raid on Wadih el Hage's home in Kenya; letter found on computer; he was told to leave the country.
Informant walked into US Embassy Nairobi claiming seven Arabs at Al Haramain linked to bin Laden group.
By this date Kenyan police arrested nine Arabs connected to the Al Haramain charity and seized files; later deported.
Mustafa Mahmoud Said Ahmed warned the US Embassy in Nairobi of a truck bomb plan.
Diplomatic Security and Foreign Buildings team conducted security review in Nairobi.
Simultaneous bombings of US embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam.
Mob of 10,000 Pakistanis stormed the US Embassy in Islamabad over rumors of American troops in Mecca; two Americans and two Pakistanis died.
US cruise missile strikes on bin Laden, which failed to kill him and raised his stature (after embassy bombings).
Wadih el Hage born in Sidon, Lebanon.
El Hage came to the US to attend the University of Southwestern Louisiana.
Al Kifah leader Mustafa Shalabi disappeared and was later found murdered on the day El Hage arrived in New York.
El Hage moved to Kenya.
El Hage searched for Banshiri's body at the Lake Victoria ferry disaster.
El Hage met Muhammed Atef in Pakistan and sent coded fax from Kenya.
Police raided El Hage's Nairobi home; he was questioned and told to leave Kenya.
El Hage testified to grand jury denying knowing Odeh.
El Hage arrested in Arlington, TX and charged with perjury.
Khalfan Khamis Mohamed arrested at Cape Town airport and sent to New York.
East African embassy bombings in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam.
Earliest date by which bin Laden, al Qaeda and affiliates showed interest in acquiring WMD agents or weapons, according to the report.
Mamdouh Mahmud Salim allegedly approved a scheme to obtain enriched uranium but was offered low-grade reactor fuel and 'Red Mercury' scam material.
Al-Hayat claimed bin Laden had acquired two or more nuclear weapons from former-Soviet Central Asian countries.
Yosef Bodansky claimed bin Laden had up to 20 suitcase nuclear bombs from Chechen rebels.
Bin Laden said in an interview that seeking WMD is a religious duty.
George J. Tenet statement to the Senate Armed Services Committee quoting bin Laden on WMD.
Bin Laden told Time magazine it would be a sin for Muslims not to try to possess such weapons.
Bin Laden interviewed by ABC's John Miller about acquiring chemical and nuclear weapons.
Bomb in shopping mall near the Kremlin killed 1, injured over 40.
Bomb in building housing Russian servicemen and families killed 64.
Apartment block bomb in Pechatniki killed 94.
Bomb at Kashirskoye Highway apartment block killed 118.
Truck bomb outside apartment building killed 18.
UK magistrate ordered extradition of Khalid al-Fawwaz to the US.
Mahrez Amduni captured in Turkey with Bosnian passport after CIA tip-off.
Putin said bin Laden's followers were involved in Dagestan and Chechnya fighting.
Sheehan met Indian officials; US then asked Pakistan to distance itself from bin Laden and Harkat-ul Ansar.
Abdul Rahim Muslim Dost offered 5 million Afghanis reward for assassination of Clinton.
Milliyet reported six bin Laden followers in Turkey planning bomb attacks on US/UK missions.
Rockets apparently launched by Taliban struck a Pakistani village near bin Laden's suspected hideout.
US, backed by Russia, introduced UN Security Council draft resolution for air embargo and financial sanctions on Taliban.
Khalfan Khamis Mohamed arrested at Cape Town airport and flown to New York by FBI.
Sharif sent ISI chief Ziauddin to Kandahar to demand closure of training camps.
Sharif and Ziauddin traveled to Dubai for talks with UAE leaders.
UN Security Council voted 15-0 for sanctions on Taliban if bin Laden not handed over.
Taliban rejected UN demand to hand over bin Laden.
Sheehan met Taliban representative Abdul Hakeem Mujahid in New York.
Mujahid met Karl Inderfurth in Washington.
Wakil Ahmad Muttawakil appointed Afghan Foreign Minister.
Ramadan began amid fears of new bin Laden operations; Pakistani intelligence raided Peshawar safe houses and arrested Iraqi, Saudi and Bosnian men with forged documents.
Administration officials said bin Laden ordered attack on American targets in the Persian Gulf; learned via eavesdropping.
Germany extradited Mamdouh Mahmud Salim to the US.
Bin Laden summoned reporters from The News, Time, ABC News to his Helmand encampment.
Time interview: bin Laden said 'our job is to instigate' and defended acquiring WMD.
Bin Laden told ABC's John Miller he denied involvement in embassy bombings but respected two suspects; told Bakhtar he was 'innocent' but 'not sorry'.
FBI release offered $5 million reward for five more embassy bombing suspects.
Sunday Times reported bin Laden rebuilt camps destroyed 20 Aug 1998 and was building headquarters in Kunduz caves.
Bin Laden called on Muslims to kill American and British nationals in retaliation for air strikes on Iraq.
The News reported Prince Salman offered $267,000 to Siddiq Anmad to kill bin Laden; Saudi denied on 27 Dec.
Hawad reported Masood met US officials in Tajikistan and received $5 million for bin Laden's arrest; Masood denied.
Indian police arrested Sayed Abu Nasir with 2 kg RDX for plot against US Embassy New Delhi and consulates in Madras and Calcutta.
Asharq al-Awsat reported Mohammad Atef denied involvement in embassy bombings.
Malaysia arrested seven Afghans with forged Italian passports and an Italian supplier at Bayan Lepas airport, en route to London.
Time and Newsweek published interviews with bin Laden on instigation, WMD acquisition, American taxpayers as targets.
US Attorney's office filed most complete indictment of bin Laden and 11 others.
Indian police arrested four suspected of plotting to bomb US Embassy New Delhi and consulates in Madras and Calcutta.

The East African embassy bombings were carried out in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam. The document calls the failure to prevent them partly a matter of resource constraints and a mistaken medium-threat rating for Nairobi.
US cruise missile strikes were followed by demonstrations in Kandahar in which 8,000 Afghans vowed to defend Osama bin Laden.
Mullah Omar tells journalist Rahimullah Yusufzai there cannot be two parallel emirates in Afghanistan.
Fazul flew from Moroni, Comoros to Dubai and was never seen again.
Jamaa Islamiyya called on Muslims to besiege American embassies in Muslim countries.
US officials told western diplomats at the UN Security Council that bin Laden was linked to 18 attacks.
Criminal complaint filed against Al-'Owhali; he was returned to the US that night.
Washington Times reported FBI alert that bin Laden offered bounties to kill Americans.
Charges filed in Manhattan against former US special forces sergeant Ali Mohamed.
CIA broke up a bin Laden ring planning an attack on the US embassy in Baku.
US embassy in Dushanbe closed due to fear of terrorist attacks.
Western embassies in Kampala closed for security reasons.
Two suspected bin Laden associates arrested entering Uganda from Kenya, allegedly plotting to bomb the US embassy in Kampala.
Mamdouh Mahmud Salim arrested in Germany near Freising.
Eight Ugandans and ten Somalis arrested in Uganda over plot against US embassy in Kampala.
Mustafa Mahmoud Said Ahmed and Rashid Saleh Hemed charged with murder in Tanzanian embassy bombing.
Saudi Arabia expelled the Afghan charge d'affaires and recalled its representative from Kabul.
Seven men arrested in London by Scotland Yard, including Adel Abdel Meguid Abdel Bari and Khaled al Fawaz.
Five Egyptian Jihad militants and Khaled al Fawaz arrested in the UK.
Prince Turki bin Faisal met Mullah Mohammed Omar to persuade Afghanistan to deport bin Laden.
Federal prosecutors in New York released a 50-page indictment of four top aides to bin Laden.
Pakistan-based militant groups threaten revenge killings against Americans over the August 1998 missile strikes.
Al Hayat reports Taliban members exchanged gunfire with bin Laden's guards during February falling out.
Saudi Arabia and Taliban sign protocol on Afghan Hajj pilgrims.
Taha and Hamza agree to halt bloodshed; Zawahiri denounces ceasefire.
Inderfurth tells Senate that US convinced bin Laden planning further attacks.
Cairo trial sentences nine Jihad leaders including Zawahiri to death in absentia.
Zawahiri meets associates in Jalalabad region to reorganize Jihad.
Egypt releases about 1,200 Gamaat Islamiya members.
US Treasury ends freeze on Saleh Idris's $24 million.
Senator Hadi claims US commandos in Waziristan and Chaman searching for bin Laden.
Bin Laden tells Qatar TV his mission is to incite Muslims against American presence in Saudi Arabia.
FBI adds bin Laden to Ten Most Wanted list.
US officials tell ABC they believe bin Laden suffers from Marfan's syndrome.
Mohamed Sadeek Odeh and other al Qaeda members stayed at the Hilltop Hotel (2-6 Aug 1998).
In the first week of August Fazul Abdullah Mohammed, Al-'Owhali, Azzam and others met at 43 Rundu Estates and made final preparations for the Nairobi bombing.
Four foreigners involved in the bombings checked into a Nairobi hotel.
A security guard saw a man with two bodyguards videotaping the US Embassy from all sides; the cameraman hid the camera and left.
Fazul, Al-'Owhali, Azzam and others reconnoitered the Nairobi embassy; Saleh and al-Owhali reportedly decided to park the truck near the rear of the building.
Abdul Rahman allegedly connected the bomb to the detonation device in the garage at 43 Rundu Estates.
Mohamed Sadeek Odeh shaved his beard and obtained new clothing to travel to Afghanistan to meet bin Laden; he also walked near the US Embassy on Moi Avenue.
A conspirator in the Tanzanian bombing telephoned a counterpart in Nairobi.
The Egyptian Jihad warned the US it would soon deliver a message, and vowed revenge over deportations of Egyptians from Albania.
Mohammed Saddiq Odeh flew from Nairobi to Pakistan under an assumed name on PIA flight 746; at least two Dar es Salaam suspects left for Karachi the same day.
Fazul Badroudin was flown from Nairobi to Moroni on the day of the bombings, arranged by his son-in-law Abdallah Mohammed Fazul.
US embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam were bombed nearly simultaneously with two large TNT bombs, on the anniversary of the arrival of US troops in Saudi Arabia in 1990.

At about 9:30 AM two trucks left 43 Rundu Estates; Fazul led in a Datsun pickup and Azzam drove the bomb truck with Al-'Owhali. Al-Owhali threw a stun grenade and fled, Azzam fired at the windows and then detonated the bomb in the rear parking area.
Nairobi bombing results: 213 dead and about 4,000 injured, including 12 Americans; the adjacent Ufundi building collapsed.
After the bombing the Nairobi embassy relocated to a heavily guarded building on the outskirts of town.
African embassy bombings, which the study examines for lessons learned. This chunk does not name the cities or the attackers.
Retaliatory U.S. cruise missile strikes following the embassy bombings. The study judges they did little to solve the problem posed by bin Laden.
Nairobi and Dar es Salaam embassy bombings using TNT-laden trucks
Odeh boasted of supplying weapons that killed 18 US soldiers in Mogadishu
Odeh moved to Kenya and married in Witu
Odeh arrested by Kenyans
Al-Owhali reconnoitered Nairobi embassy
Al-Owhali contacted by Kenyan officials and subsequently arrested
Fazul departed Moroni for Dubai and disappeared
Al-Owhali met bin Laden and requested a mission
US cruise missile strikes in retaliation for the embassy bombings. They hit targets in Afghanistan and the Al Shifa plant (a night watchman was killed). Missiles overflew Pakistan.
Shortly after the strikes the Taliban tried to promulgate a policy of putting bin Laden in 'internal exile'.
Bin Laden, al Qaeda and affiliated groups' interest in acquiring WMD is said to date back at least to 1993.
Osama bin Laden born in Riyadh
Bin Laden traveled to Pakistan to help the mujahideen against the Soviet invasion
Soviets invaded Afghanistan (other sources give Dec 26)
Bin Laden decided to enter Afghanistan with construction machinery for the mujahedeen
Bin Laden left Saudi Arabia and moved to Sudan
World Trade Center bombed in New York by Arab Afghans
Bin Laden stripped of Saudi citizenship; assets frozen
Bin Laden issued Declaration of Jihad against Americans occupying the Two Holy Mosques
Bomb attacks on US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania
Cruise missile attacks in Sudan and Afghanistan
Odeh left Mombasa and moved to Witu, Kenya.
US security review team arrived in Nairobi for embassy security review.
Bill Richardson was to meet Taliban officials in Kabul reportedly offering recognition for bin Laden.
Fazul rented villa at 43 Rundu Estates, Nairobi.
Said Sayyed Salameh was arrested at Salom frontier trying to enter Egypt from Tobruk, Libya.
International Islamic Front met in Peshawar and resolved to hit US interests worldwide.
Prince Turki al-Faisal led a Saudi delegation to Kandahar seeking bin Laden's ouster or custody.
Fadhil and another suspect rented a villa in Dar es Salaam used as bomb factory.
Grand jury investigating bin Laden issued a sealed indictment.
Bin Laden interviewed on ABC's Nightline, threatening Americans.
American and Albanian agents arrested Ahmed Ibrahim al Najjar in Tirana; he was extradited to Egypt.
Planning for Kenya and Tanzania bombings began under Ali Saleh.
Al-'Owhali and Azzam filmed a martyrdom videotape claiming credit for the Army for the Liberation of Islamic Holy Places.
Al-'Owhali traveled from Lahore to Nairobi.
Fazul took Owhali to view the US Embassy in Nairobi.
Odeh, Fazul and other al Qaeda members met at Hilltop Hotel, Nairobi.
Final bombing preparations at 43 Rundu Estates.
The US General Accounting Office issued the report 'Combatting Terrorism: Observations on the Threat of Chemical and Biological Terrorism', which this document quotes.
Aum Shinrikyo used impure sarin on the Tokyo subway system.
US cruise missile strikes (discussed in earlier sections) are cited as relevant to the option of using force against bin Laden.
Bin Laden helped expel the Soviets from Afghanistan, which earned him a reputation as a war hero.
Haroun Fazil writes a letter later found on Wadih el Hage's computer, urging contact via the internet from Pakistan for information on bin Laden.
Bin Laden gives an interview to ABC, justifying terrorism and attacks on Americans, and calling the Riyadh bombers martyrs.
Bin Laden gives an interview to Time magazine saying Americans are targets.
US cruise missile strikes on Salman Farsi camp near Khost and the Al Shifa plant.
Bin Laden reportedly wins tentative approval from Sudanese leaders to develop chemical weapons.
Indictment against bin Laden alleges an al Qaeda understanding with the Government of Iraq.
Bin Laden reportedly meets the Iraqi ambassador to Turkey.
Sandy Berger tells a press conference the US knew bin Laden sought chemical weapons before the Al Shifa attack.
Bombings of the U.S. embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam prompted the Sandia study.
Aum Shinrikyo sarin attack on the Tokyo subway using punctured plastic bags.
Robert Fisk interviewed bin Laden in Afghanistan; bin Laden called US troop presence in Saudi Arabia an insult.
Bin Laden exhorted followers to strike US forces in Saudi Arabia.
Bin Laden issued Declaration of Jihad ('Ladenese Epistle') from the Hindu Kush.
Nida'ul Islam magazine quoted bin Laden on US/Israeli killings of Muslims.
Gwynne Roberts interviewed bin Laden for Dispatches.
Odeh sent to Somalia on mission for bin Laden by Wadih el Hage.
Bin Laden relocated from Jalalabad to Kandahar.
Peter Arnett's CNN interview of bin Laden declaring jihad against US government.
Pakistani commandos attacked village near Peshawar; at least 6 Arab mujahideen killed.
Pakistani commandos entered Afghanistan to capture or kill bin Laden; intercepted and disarmed by Taliban.
Bin Laden moved with family to Kandahar camp near Khost.
Saudi intelligence gave CIA and MI6 a bin Laden finance official; Jallud arrested.
Reported formation of US-backed mercenary force to abduct or kill bin Laden; vehicles seen entering Khost.
Nairobi police and FBI searched Wadih El Hage's home and seized his computer.
Wadih el Hage moved from Nairobi to Arlington, Texas; questioned by FBI.
Mohamed bin Moisalih defected via Saudi intelligence, leaving Afghanistan for Peshawar then Saudi Arabia.
Bin Laden hosted terrorist conference in Afghanistan with network leaders.
Bin Laden issued edict announcing coalition and calling for killing Americans.
International Islamic Front communique signed by Taha, Zawahiri, Mir Hamze, Fazal al Rahman Khali, Abdul Salaam Mohamed; fatwa published in Al-Quds al-Arabi.
Mob of 10,000 Pakistanis, inflamed by rumors that American troops had entered Mecca, stormed the U.S. Embassy in Islamabad; four died.
NYT reports criticism of the cruise missile attacks as making bin Laden a hero, from Pakistani, Sudanese and US officials.
Embassy bombings in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam, cited as not prevented despite warnings.
Car bomb outside OPM/SANG headquarters in Riyadh killed 7 and injured 42.
actors: Office of the Program Manager/Saudi Arabian National Guard

events.description: Hassan al Srihi extradited from Pakistan to Saudi Arabia.
Khobar Towers bombing killed 19 US servicemen.
Hani al-Sayegh arrested by Canadian authorities and deported to the US.
Al-Quds al-Arabi published bin Laden's 12-page statement calling for holy war.
Secret grand jury investigation of bin Laden began in New York.
Bin Laden interviewed in eastern Afghanistan by CNN's Peter Arnett.
Saudi delegation led by Prince Turki visited Kandahar to seek bin Laden's ouster or custody.
Two representatives of wealthy Saudis visited bin Laden and paid him not to operate in Saudi Arabia.
Mohammed Shawky al-Islambouli went to Peshawar.
Extremist 'parallel' conclave in Tehran attended by Jibril, Mugnieh, Salem and Mohamed Ali.
Bin Laden met Iranian intelligence officials in Tehran.
International Islamic Front communiqué signed in Afghanistan, including Bangladesh Jihad chief.
Reports bin Laden attended an Islamic gathering near Dhaka.
Bangladesh police seized pro-bin Laden leaflets and arrested six people.
International Islamic Front published a communique in Afghanistan signed by Taha, Zawahiri, Mir Hamze, Khali and Abdul Salaam Mohamed; a fatwa to kill Americans was published in Al-Quds al-Arabi.
Bin Laden summoned by a furious Mullah Omar after his press conference.
President Clinton decided on a two-track effort: commando extrication preparations and pressing the Taliban to surrender bin Laden; US teams sent to Peshawar.
UN Ambassador Bill Richardson led the first high-level US delegation to Afghanistan since the early 1970s; Taliban refused to hand over bin Laden.
Fatwa by the Ulema Union of Afghanistan labeling the US Army enemies of Islam was published in Al-Quds al-Arabi at bin Laden's behest.
Bin Laden held a press conference in Khost attended by Atef and Al-'Owhali, repeating intent to kill Americans.
International Islamic Front for Jihad Against Jews and Crusaders held a news conference in Peshawar announcing the coalition.
actors: World Islamic Front for Jihad Against Jews and Crusaders

events.description: Bin Laden gave an ABC News interview to John Miller, threatening Americans.
Bin Laden set up a network in Albania under cover of a Saudi humanitarian agency.
Mahmud Sayyid Jaballah sent to find recruits in Baku, setting up a network across Afghanistan, Bosnia, Albania and the UK.
Raids in Tirana seized plans to bomb the US Embassy; at least five Egyptians arrested and deported to Egypt with US help.
Over 200 US military personnel sent to Albania to evacuate dependents and guard the residential compound.
The Ambassador cabled Washington requesting support for a new chancery in Nairobi; the request was denied.
A security assessment team from Washington visited the Nairobi embassy to review security.
The Ambassador sent letters to the Secretary of State (April) and Under Secretary Cohen (May) restating security concerns and the need for a new chancery.
A truck bomb exploded at the US Embassy at 36 Laibon Road, Dar es Salaam, at 10:39 AM after being blocked by an embassy water tanker; 11 dead, 85+ injured. Detonated by 'Ahmed the German'.
Simultaneous bombing of the US Embassy in Nairobi; combined African bombings originally estimated at 265 dead and 5,000+ injured; Kenya later revised its dead from 247 to 213.
Minutes after the Dar es Salaam blast, an operative in a Suzuki Samurai photographed the embassy ruins while leaving.
The relocated Nairobi embassy operated from a building on the outskirts of town with a heavily guarded approach.
Bombings of the U.S. embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam.
U.S. retaliatory cruise missile strikes after the embassy bombings.
Aum Shinrikyo sarin attack on the Tokyo subway, using punctured plastic bags.
Taliban spokesman Muttawakil dismissed reports of bin Laden planning attacks as hollow rumors.
Taliban announced new restrictions on bin Laden: satellite phone shut off, barred from media.
Taliban replaced bin Laden's bodyguards with ten intelligence/foreign ministry guards; he was expelled from Kandahar to the countryside.
Mullah Omar and spokesman Tayyab announced bin Laden had disappeared.
French police arrested Said Laidoni, militant believed linked to bin Laden.
Car bombings in Tashkent killed 15 and injured over 100; linked to Islamic extremists.
Karl Inderfurth met Taliban representative Abdul Mujahid in Washington to press on bin Laden.
Al Hayat reported bin Laden was at Tora Bora base near Jalalabad.
SCIRI's Bayan Jaber claimed Saddam offered to shelter bin Laden and that he had settled in Iraq.
USA Today reported US intelligence prevented at least 7 bin Laden vehicle bomb attacks on US facilities since August 1998.
Al Hayat reported Taliban delegation including Mullah Abdul Jalil visited bin Laden in Jalalabad (Taliban denied on 25 Feb).
General Henry Shelton refused to rule out new bombing raids against bin Laden.
Abu Hamza Al Masri threatened to blow up Western aircraft using balloon-borne 'flying mines'.
Pakistan-based groups threatened revenge killings of Americans over August 1998 missile strikes.
Al Hayat reported Taliban militia and bin Laden's guards exchanged gunfire during the February falling out.
About 70 Tomahawk cruise missiles launched against Zhawar Kili complex, Al-Badr and other camps near Khost; about 24 reportedly killed, mostly Pakistani recruits.
Strike on Harkatul Jihad Al-Islami, Jamiatul Mujahideen and Harkatul Ansar camps; at least 7 HUA members killed; Bin Laden survived.
Six Tomahawk missiles struck Al Shifa Pharmaceutical plant near Khartoum; night watchman killed.
HUA responsible for kidnappings and presumed murders of four Western tourists in Kashmir.
State Department listed Harakat Ansar as a terrorist organization; it renamed itself.
Scotland Yard arrests Hani al Sibai in London.
Salameh extradited from Tirana.
East African embassy bombings in Kenya and Tanzania linked to bin Laden.
US places a spy inside bin Laden's organization who gives information on the Kenya embassy attack team.
Truck bomb attacks on the U.S. embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam; most deaths were Kenyans in the building next to the Nairobi embassy, which collapsed.
In Nairobi, the bomber failed to penetrate the embassy perimeter because local guards refused to open the gates.
In Dar es Salaam, the bomber was stopped by guards and blocked by an embassy water truck.
The Accountability Review Boards published their report on the Nairobi and Dar es Salaam embassy bombings.
Eight Ugandans and ten Somalis arrested on suspicion of planning a one-ton truck bomb attack on the US Embassy in Kampala; explosives and dump truck seized.
Muruli Mukasa said 18 suspects were held and the Kampala plot, timed with the 7 Aug bombings, was foiled.
US suspended Peace Corps program in Uganda over safety concerns.
Bin Laden expelled from Sudan and moved to Afghanistan; Jebel Kadr farm given to a UN project and his company auctioned.
Ferry Bukoba sank in Lake Victoria; Abu Ubaidah al Banshiri drowned.
Bin Laden interviewed by Robert Fisk, said American presence in Saudi Arabia is an insult.
Bin Laden issued the Declaration of Jihad (Ladenese Epistle) from the Hindu Kush.
Taliban handed newly captured Khost camps to Harkat in autumn 1996.
Bin Laden press conference announcing jihad against America, angering Mullah Omar.
Odeh traveled from Nairobi to Karachi, detained on way to Kabul.
Clinton's advisors ordered Pentagon and CIA to list bin Laden-linked targets.
Al-'Owhali taken into custody by Kenyan officials.
Advisors briefed Clinton on bin Laden's WMD interest.
Odeh flown back to Nairobi.
Fazul flew from Nairobi to Comoros.
Investigators raided Hill Top Hotel.
White House meeting chose to attack Afghan camps, Al Shifa and a tannery.
Clinton removed tannery from target list.
US added bin Laden to Treasury funds seizure list.
Raid on Wadih el Hage's home in Kenya; a letter found on his computer; he was told to leave the country.
An informant walked into the US Embassy in Nairobi alleging that Al Haramain Foundation workers had bin Laden connections.
Kenyan police arrested nine Arabs connected to the Al Haramain charity and seized its files.
The nine charity employees were deported in late 1997 and the investigation dropped.
Mustafa Mahmoud Said Ahmed warned the US Embassy in Nairobi of a truck bomb plot and admitted taking part in surveillance.
A Diplomatic Security and Foreign Building Office team arrived in Nairobi to conduct a security review.
Simultaneous East African embassy bombings, which warnings and disruption had failed to prevent.
Bombings of the US embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam. Most deaths were Kenyans in the building next to the Nairobi embassy.
A planned bombing of a US installation in Albania was prevented before the embassy attacks.
After the bombings, the US escalated its campaign against bin Laden and apprehended a number of perpetrators.
Al Hayat reported bin Laden left his Jalalabad hideout for a secret location under Taliban supervision with Atef and Zawahiri; Jang reported fortified bunkers guarded by 450 Arabs.
Mohammad Siddiq Kanju said a US missile strike on Afghanistan was a danger.
Traces of plastic explosives found in a vehicle outside US embassy in Antananarivo.
Bin Laden announced he would leave Afghanistan; a Taliban spokesman denied it.
Report that Islamic Jihad members bought anthrax from an East Asian source; al-Najar confessed details.
Yosef Bodansky claimed bin Laden had up to 20 suitcase nukes bought from Chechen rebels.
Shamil Basayev launched a Muslim rebel offensive in Dagestan on the anniversary of the embassy bombings.
Report that two US planes with commandos landed in Islamabad and Quetta; US State Department issued travel warning for Pakistan.
Taliban rejected claims of bin Laden training camps in Afghanistan.
Taliban and US diplomats held regular meetings negotiating bin Laden's surrender.
Fazlur Rehman at Chaman warned against US attack and vowed to fight alongside the Taliban.
Mullah Mohammed Rabbani warned US not to use force to capture bin Laden.
Over 4,000 Islamic activists including Jamiat-Ulema-Islami members marched in Lahore supporting bin Laden.
Truck bomb near Mullah Omar's home in Kandahar killed about 40, including relatives of Omar.
El Mouaz Hallali arrived in Yemen to reorganize Tarek el Fodhil's Jihad and Aden Islamic Army.
Clinton wrote to Iranian President Khatami seeking support against terrorism.
Bomb in shopping mall near the Kremlin killed 1.
Bomb in Buinaksk, Dagestan killed 64.
Bomb in Pechatniki, Moscow apartment block killed 94.
Bomb at Kashirskoye Highway, Moscow killed 118.
Truck bomb in Volgodonsk killed 18.
UK magistrate ordered extradition of Khalid al-Fawwaz to the US over embassy bombing conspiracy with al Qaeda.
Embassy bombings in East Africa, which bin Laden said he instigated.
US cruise missile attacks on training camps near Khost and the Al Shifa plant.
Hafiz Shabir Ahmad killed in Kashmir; farewell letter found on body.
Fatwa by Imam Abdur Rahman al-Hudhayfi opposing American military presence in Saudi Arabia.
Haroun Fazil wrote letters warning of the cell's security compromise, later found in Wadih el Hage's computer.
Bin Laden Time magazine interview on targeting Americans.
Bassam Alamoush speech at Arab conference in Chicago.
Report that bin Laden had three businesses in the Philippines and a Filipino wife; rebels say it is his brother-in-law.
Security forces foiled attempt to smuggle arms into Mindanao.
Julabbi acknowledged MILF funding from sympathizers abroad.
Report that Abu Sayyaf and MILF expected a large arms shipment, funded largely from Afghanistan.
MILF admitted receiving bin Laden aid for a decade, refused since 1998.
Salamat Hashim told Reuters bin Laden funded mosques/schools before 1984, no weapons.
Tanjungperak port monitored MV Alkeen Perdaba, suspected of carrying 3,000 anti-tank rockets from Afghanistan to Moros.
Bin Laden banned from travel in Saudi Arabia for plans for a jihad front in South Yemen.
Iraq invaded Kuwait; bin Laden wrote to the King offering mujahedeen to defend the country.
U.S. troops began arriving in Saudi Arabia.
Saudi authorities issued arrest warrant for bin Laden.
Bin Laden issued Open Letter to King Fahd.
Fighting broke out along the Dagestan border with Chechnya.
Muslim rebel offensive launched in Dagestan by Shamil Basayev on first anniversary of the East Africa embassy bombings.
Islamic guerillas declared Dagestan an independent state.
Safir Ahmed met bin Laden in Jalalabad.
Bomb in a shopping mall near the Kremlin killed 1 and injured over 40.
Apartment block bombing in Pechatniki, Moscow killed 94.
Rushailo said police seized explosives, detonators and firearms in an anti-terror sweep.
Said el-Maban allegedly traveled to Chechnya and paid warlords $200,000 for the Moscow bombings.
Mahmud Sayyid Jaballah asked to find recruits in Baku and set up a network.
Five Islamic militants arrested in London; Khaled al Fawaz also arrested.
London Evening Standard reported bin Laden planning to kidnap a high-profile US national via London connections.
Gathering of Islamic movements in London at Friend's House; Omar Bakri Muhammad issued warning.
The 20 August 1998 cruise missile strikes are referred to as the earlier discussion of the pros and cons of using force, including against bin Laden.
London Evening Standard reported bin Laden planned to kidnap a high-profile US national via London connections; US on high alert.
Gathering of Islamic movements at Friend's House in London; Omar Bakri Muhammad warned of fundamentalist terrorism if six militants were extradited.
Abu Hamza denied links to five UK nationals arrested in Yemen on 24 December.
Al Hayat reported Abu Hamza threatened to blow up Western aircraft using balloon 'flying mines'.
Three men held after anti-terrorist raids in London; Supporters of Sharia said Abu Hamza had been arrested.
Six westerners kidnapped in Kashmir by HUA affiliates; Hans Christian Ostro beheaded.
US designated HUA a foreign terrorist organization.
Sayed Abu Nasir and six others entered India from Bangladesh and scouted US consulates in Madras and Calcutta.
Jayalalitha warned some 200 Afghan-trained bin Laden supporters were roaming in Tamil Nadu.
Indian police arrested Sayed Abu Nasir at New Delhi station with 2 kg RDX over plot against US embassy/consulates.
Indian police arrested four people suspected of plotting to bomb US Embassy in New Delhi and consulates.
US counterterrorism team arrived in India to investigate the plot.
Mohammad Akbar Bhatt arrested with aide in New Delhi; explosives seized.
Taliban handed Khost camps to Harkat in autumn 1996.
Sudan reportedly acquired and used chemical weapons as early as 1992.
Bin Laden reportedly won tentative Sudanese approval to develop chemical weapons.
Indictment against bin Laden alleges al Qaeda-Iraq understanding.
CIA agent collected soil sample near Al Shifa factory containing EMPTA.
CIA issued first intelligence report on Al Shifa.
New CIA report assessed Sudan-bin Laden chemical weapons connection.
State Department analysts skeptical of CIA report on Al Shifa.
US cruise missile attack on Al Shifa plant.
John Gannon stated bin Laden had ties to Al Shifa and sought poison gas.
Small Group of advisors met Clinton about bin Laden WMD.
Al-Hayat quoted Ahmad Salama Mabrouk on bin Laden's group's weapons and planned operations.
actors: International Islamic Front for Fighting Jews and Crusaders

events.description: Islamic Jihad members reportedly bought anthrax from an East Asian source.
Late 1993: al Qaida effort to obtain enriched uranium approved by Salim.
Al-Hayat claimed bin Laden acquired nuclear weapons from Central Asia.
Shooting and firebombing of tourist bus outside Egyptian Museum; 9 Germans and driver killed, 26 injured.
Two men sentenced to death for the killings.
Islamic Group attack on tourists in the Valley of the Kings near Luxor; 58 tourists and 4 Egyptians killed.
Urs von Daeniken said Egypt believed Mustafa Hamza ordered the Luxor attack from Sudan with bin Laden funding.
Gamaa Al Islamiya announced it would stop targeting tourism and foreign tourists.
Jihad statement described cease-fire with US and Israel as a step back.
Jamma Islamiyya called on Moslems to besiege American embassies.
Mutassar al-Zayat said the group cut ties with bin Laden in July.
Military court in Egypt began trial of 107 alleged Islamic Jihad members.
Islamic Group announced peaceful campaign in response to Abdel-Rahman's call.
Military court sentenced 9 to death in absentia and 11 to life, including al-Naggar; Zawahri among defendants.
Seven Al-Jihad militants extradited to Egypt from three Arab countries.
Egypt arrested 23 suspected Taleat Fatah militants.
Military court sentenced 20 militants over plot to assassinate Mubarak.
Knife-wielding militant slightly wounded Mubarak in Port Said and was shot dead.
FBI found Ramzi Yousef in Su Casa guesthouse in Islamabad.
Arab Afghans bombed Egyptian Embassy in Islamabad; 17 killed; Egyptian Islamic Jihad claimed it.
Arafat attended OIC summit; plot to kill him revealed by ISI informer.
ISI raided Pabi refugee camp near Jallozai.
Bin Laden's faxed threats from Kandahar led US to barricade its embassy in Pakistan.
Over 4,000 activists marched in Lahore protesting US actions against bin Laden.
Sheehan testified Pakistan supported militant training.
Lashkar-e-Tayyaba conference in Muridke.
Security forces foiled arms smuggling into Mindanao.
Raids in Tirana seized material including plans to bomb US Embassy; at least 5 Egyptians arrested and deported to Egypt with US help.
Cairo trial sentences nine Egyptian Jihad leaders including Zawahiri to death in absentia.
Reports Albania continued rounding up and expelling people linked to bin Laden.
Odeh moved to Mombasa and set up fish business; El Hage moved from Khartoum to Nairobi; Ali Mohamed entered US Embassy Nairobi on surveillance.
US Embassy in Sudan evacuated and relocated to Nairobi.
Nairobi police and FBI searched El Hage's home, seizing papers and computer revealing East African cell letter.
El Hage told to leave Kenya and returned to the US with his wife.
Tipster at US Embassy Nairobi alleged Al Haramain Foundation links to bin Laden; nine Arabs arrested by 31 October and later deported.
Mustafa Mahmoud Said Ahmed warned the US Embassy of a planned truck bombing; extra guards posted and letter sent to Albright.
Odeh moved from Mombasa to Witu.
Security review team arrives in Nairobi; bin Laden faxed threats from Kandahar causing US to barricade embassy in Pakistan.
Richardson scheduled to meet Taliban officials in Kabul, reportedly offering recognition for surrender of bin Laden.
Five Egyptian Jihad militants and Khaled al Fawaz arrested in the U.K.
Prince Turki bin Faisal met privately with Mullah Omar to persuade the Taliban to deport bin Laden.
Federal prosecutors in New York released a 50-page indictment of four top aides to bin Laden.
All US missions in Saudi Arabia closed for four days after information of a threat to the US Embassy in Riyadh.
Al Hayat reported the Taliban might put bin Laden on trial for the 1996 Khobar Towers bombing.
Jayalalitha warned ~200 Afghan-trained bin Laden supporters were roaming southern India and linked bin Laden agents to Coimbatore bombings.
Mohamed Abed Abdel Aal of Jamaa Islamiyya arrested at a hotel in Bogota after arriving from Quito.
Taliban ambassador Abdelhakim Mujahid said it would be very difficult to push bin Laden out of Afghanistan.
The Taliban invited outsiders to provide evidence of bin Laden's terrorism links to the Taliban supreme court.
Lashkar-e-Taiba organized a gathering of 50,000 youths near Lahore with anti-US banners.
Federal jury in New York issued a 238-count indictment charging bin Laden and Mohammed Atef; State Department announced $5 million rewards.
US embassy in Riyadh and consulates in Jiddah and Dhahran to close 11-14 Nov over a possible terrorist attack.
Taliban Chief Justice Noor Mohammed Saqib closed an inquiry and pronounced bin Laden a free man.
Austria tightened security at US missions in Vienna after indications of a planned attack.
Four Afghan men hired to assassinate bin Laden were ambushed and killed near his hideout in southern Afghanistan.
Munich court approved extradition to the US of Mamdouh Mahmud Salim, alleged bin Laden finance chief.
Chechen Foreign Ministry official arrived in Kandahar to discuss diplomatic relations with the Taliban.
Bin Laden reportedly met the Iraqi ambassador to Turkey.
Nawaz Sharif admitted talks with US officials on Pakistan helping seize bin Laden; CS-1 plea reported.
Police raided a guest house in Islamabad on tips bin Laden might be visiting.
Police conducted two raids in Lahore on tips bin Laden might be visiting.
Khabrain reported American commandos returned from a futile two-week operation in Afghanistan to arrest bin Laden.
US embassies in Gulf states warned of possible attacks after bin Laden conversations monitored; curfew in Bahrain.
Five men indicted for the Dar es Salaam embassy bombing; rewards of up to $5 million offered.
Ramadan began amid fears of new al Qaeda operations; Pakistani intelligence raids in Peshawar found Zainul Abideen's safe houses.
International Islamic Front communiqué issued in Afghanistan, signed by Sheik Abdul Salaam Mohamed.
44 people arrested over foiled plot to kill poet Shamshur Rahman in Dhaka; Harakat ul-Jihad members.
Rally of 15,000 in Dhaka supported bin Laden and the Taliban.
Austrian police arrested Adel Assayed Abdul Kudus in Vienna.
Mahmud Sayyid Jaballah asked to recruit in Baku and built a network.
CIA broke up bin Laden ring planning attack on US embassy in Baku; Mabrouk arrested.
New security measures introduced around US facilities in Gulf countries after intercepted bin Laden plot discussions.
Car bombings in Tashkent killed 15 people.
Indictment against bin Laden alleging al Qaeda–Iraq understanding.
Kuwaiti police arrested an Arab man at Al-Salmi crossing carrying forged Kuwaiti citizenship certificate with bin Laden's photo.
Clinton met Pakistani PM Nawaz Sharif in Washington.
Observer reported bin Laden seen near Jalalabad; families left fearing US missile strike.
Clinton signed executive order imposing sanctions on the Taliban for harboring bin Laden.
Mullah Omar told Afghan Islamic Press he did not know where bin Laden was.
Mutawakil said Taliban ready for talks with US; State Dept's James Foley said US willing to negotiate.
Two Egyptian men arrested in London linked by fingerprints to 1998 embassy bombings conspiracy.
Mutawakel interviewed in Asharq Al-Awsat during UAE visit on possible third-country trial of bin Laden.
US State Department travel advisory warned bin Laden supporters planned attacks on US interests in Pakistan.
Sunday Times reported Takfiris seeking to kill bin Laden; fatwa seen near Peshawar.
US Embassy in Maputo closed over threat; reopened 30 July.
Karl Inderfurth met Taliban representatives; Omar then refused extradition of bin Laden.
Iranian radio reported US commander and elite troops landed at Peshawar airport to capture bin Laden and moved to Waziristan.
Jamiat-i Ulema-i Islam demonstrations in Pakistan; US Embassy in Chad closed over bomb threat.
Taliban reportedly detained four men hunting bin Laden who had contact with US troops in Peshawar.
Al Hayat reported bin Laden left Jalalabad hideout for secret location with Atef and Zawahiri.
Traces of plastic explosives found in vehicle outside US embassy in Antananarivo.
Bin Laden established guesthouse Baitul'ansar in Peshawar; Jihad Service Bureau formed by Abdullah Azzam.
Bin Laden decided to have his own camps inside Afghanistan; fought Soviets at Jaji.
Bin Laden reportedly led an offensive against Soviet troops in the battle of Shaban.
Bin Laden's complex named Al-Qa'edah and documentation of mujahedeen improved.
Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan completed.
Bin Laden returned to Saudi Arabia.
Sadat assassinated by Egyptian Islamic Jihad; assassin Khaled al-Islambouli.
Mohammed Shawky al-Islambouli made his way to Peshawar.
Mohammed Shawky al-Islambouli sentenced to death in absentia by Egypt.
Egyptian Islamic Jihad car-bomb attempts on PM Atef Sidqi and Interior Minister Hassan al-Alfi.
Attempted assassination of Mubarak in Addis Ababa by Egyptian radicals based in Sudan.
Egyptian officials uncovered Islamic Jihad plot to assassinate Mubarak; informant said bin Laden helped fund.
21 suspected Islamic Group militants arrested for planning rocket attack on Alexandria military target.
Shooting and firebombing of tourist bus at Egyptian Museum, Cairo; 9 Germans and driver killed.
Two men sentenced to death for the bus attack killings.
Khalid al-Fawwaz arrested in the UK.
UK magistrate ordered al-Fawwaz's extradition to the US over embassy bombing conspiracy.
FBI raided Nosair's New Jersey home, finding military documents supplied by Ali Mohamed.
Ali Mohamed escorted bin Laden from Pakistan/Afghanistan to Sudan.
Ali Mohamed entered the US Embassy in Nairobi on a surveillance mission.
Zawahiri traveled to Peshawar.
Wadih el Hage sent coded fax from Kenya to Orlando co-conspirator after meeting Atef in Pakistan.
Mamdouh Mahmud Salim allegedly approved a scheme to obtain enriched uranium.
US cruise missile strikes (code-named Infinite Reach) hit the Al Shifa plant and Afghan targets.
Clinton signed E.O. 13099 freezing assets of bin Laden and associates.
Clinton televised address linking bin Laden to attacks and plots.
Mullah Omar told Rahimullah Yusufzai there cannot be two parallel emirates in Afghanistan.
Abdallah Mohammed Fazul flew from Moroni, Comoros to Dubai and was never seen again.
Jamma Islamiyya called on Muslims to besiege American embassies.
At UN Security Council briefing, US officials said bin Laden was linked to 18 attacks.
Clinton said he stayed awake to ensure no night shift at the chemical plant.
Intelligence officials briefed Ambassador Bushnell on the presence of the terrorist group in Nairobi; no specific threat evidence.
Embassy bombings in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam; bombers failed to penetrate the perimeter, but vehicle bombs caused major damage.
US cruise missile strikes failed to kill bin Laden and boosted his image among Pakistan's Islamic hardliners.
Pakistani Deputy Foreign Minister Kanju criticized the cruise missile attacks as inflating bin Laden.
Taliban UN representative and Karl Inderfurth discussed UN sanctions and bin Laden.
Taliban deny reports they will hand over bin Laden.
Bin Laden reportedly offered in a letter to Omar to leave Afghanistan under two conditions.
Prince Nayef said the bin Laden case was grossly inflated and not worthy of the UN Security Council.
Muttawakil said Omar assured bin Laden he would not be handed over.
Taliban reportedly disarmed Arab Afghan units and moved camps, including Dronthe, toward Kabul.
Michael Sheehan told a Senate subcommittee Pakistan was supporting militant training and Kashmiri militants.
Taliban accused the U.S. of bad faith in handover talks.
Three-day Lashkar-e-Tayyaba conference began at Muridke, with Hafiz Saeed speaking.
Mullah Omar warned Americans of 'surprises' if UN sanctions were imposed.
Group began calling itself Al Qaeda.
Mamdouh Mahmud Salim arrested in Germany.
Bin Laden interviews published by Time and Newsweek: says job is to instigate terrorism, WMD acquisition a duty.
Bin Laden renews call for attacks on Americans, Jews and Christians in broadcast interview.
US Attorney's office files indictment of bin Laden and 11 others.
Indian police arrest four suspected of plotting to bomb US Embassy in New Delhi and consulates in Madras and Calcutta.
French agents arrest Said Laidouni.
Reports of bin Laden plan to kidnap a US national via London connections; documents seized at Khalid Al-Fawaz's home.
UN Security Council demands Taliban stop sheltering terrorists.
Bin Laden prays publicly with Taliban leaders.
Richard Clarke says US foiled truck-bomb attacks on at least two US embassies.
Uruguayan police arrest three Islamic Group members in Chuy; fourth arrested 3 Feb, after CIA tip.
Said Mohkles arrested in South America.
Trial of 107 Islamic fundamentalists begins in Egypt.
Bin Laden again issues fatwa declaring jihad against the USA.
George J. Tenet tells Senate Armed Services Committee of activity similar to pre-embassy bombing.
Inderfurth meets Sartaj Aziz and Jalil Akhund in Islamabad, delivers letter demanding bin Laden.
FBI agents arrest Ali Mohfoudh Salim in Kenya.
Kenyan court in Mombasa blocks extradition of Ali Mohfoudh Salim.
Derek Fatchett meets Abdul Rahman Zahid in Islamabad about bin Laden.
Taliban say they would try bin Laden given evidence but not expel him.
Fight in Kandahar between bin Laden's bodyguards and Taliban officers; Taliban restrict bin Laden, take phone.
Reports bin Laden seen near Iranian border or crossing into Iran at Torghundi; denied by Iran.
Taliban replace bin Laden's bodyguards with intelligence/foreign ministry staff and expel him from Kandahar.
US launched Tomahawk cruise missiles at the Al Shifa plant near Khartoum.
Clinton called off a planned attack on a tannery in Sudan hours before the strike.
CIA agent collected soil sample near Al Shifa containing EMPTA traces.
Senior US officials admitted no direct evidence linking bin Laden to Al Shifa at the time of the strikes.
Bin Laden reportedly won tentative Sudanese approval to develop chemical weapons.
Informant reported two Khartoum sites possibly involved in chemical weapons and mentioned Al Shifa's high security.
US intelligence said bin Laden had Marfan's syndrome and was in advanced stages of planning another attack.
Federal grand jury in New York indicted al-Zawahiri and al-Fawwaz over the East Africa embassy bombings.

Counterterrorism officials said bin Laden's network had targeted US diplomatic facilities and he was in final stages of planning an attack; embassies in Mozambique, Senegal and Ghana were of most concern.
US temporarily closed six African embassies over surveillance concerns; reopened 28 June except Madagascar.
UK announced temporary closure of its embassies in Gambia, Madagascar, Namibia and Senegal.
Yasser Tawfiq el-Siri warned Islamic fundamentalists would attack US facilities and advised the UK to distance itself from the US.
Bin Laden reportedly seen in a truck convoy toward Farmihadda south of Jalalabad.
US Treasury and NSC officials traveled to the UAE to discuss bin Laden's relationship with Dubai Islamic Bank and Qatari warning to Khaled Shaikh Mohammad.
Attempt to arrest Khaled Shaikh Mohammad in Doha failed after he disappeared.
State Department banned travel to Pakistan after reports of terrorist plots.
Mustafa Elnore arrested and charged with lying about his relationships with terrorists.
FBI halted public tours of its headquarters over a possible bin Laden operative attack.
Taliban launched massive offensive north of Kabul against the Northern Alliance with Pakistani volunteers and bin Laden-loyal Arabs.
Kuwaiti police arrested an Arab man at Al-Salmi carrying a forged citizenship certificate with bin Laden's photo.
Observer reported bin Laden at Hadda farm near Jalalabad; local families fled fearing a US strike.

key_claims: Bin Laden is not a new threat but a capable adversary whose al Qaeda organization has exploitable weaknesses.
Bin Laden has had significant state support rather than being a freelance agent.
Bin Laden is more a terrorist sponsor and instigator than an arms-carrying terrorist.
The 20 August 1998 cruise missile strikes did little to solve the bin Laden problem and may have done more harm than good.
Radiological dispersion is judged the greatest WMD risk, followed by low-end chemical or biological agents; al Qaeda has so far been unable to acquire or employ WMD.
The root cause of the Islamic militant threat is widespread discontent in the Islamic world, so diplomatic options offer the most effective long-term reduction.
Bin Laden is more a sponsor of terrorism and a guerrilla warlord than a traditional terrorist, commanding about 3,000 fighters and influencing many thousands more.
Bin Laden has enjoyed significant state support, and Afghanistan offered him sanctuary without being a clear nation-state backer of his attacks.
Al Qaeda is a non-hierarchical organization with global recruitment, front companies, large bases and extensive funds.
Al Qaeda's dependence on large bases, international travel, communications and financial networks makes it vulnerable to surveillance and interception.
The East African al Qaeda cell and its members were known and under intense scrutiny before the 7 Aug 1998 embassy bombings.
Bin Laden's death would likely make him a martyr-symbol, so the threat would not die with him.
US authorities knew of the East African al-Qa'ida cell and had it under surveillance before the 7 August 1998 embassy bombings.
The embassy bombings generated enormous publicity for bin Laden and made him a worldwide icon.
The 20 August 1998 cruise missile strikes may have driven bin Laden into better-protected bases and bolstered al-Qa'ida recruitment.
The strikes tarnished the Taliban's image and may have pushed them to constrain bin Laden, as in the publicized 'internal exile'.
Al-Qa'ida and bin Laden have sought chemical, biological and nuclear weapons since at least 1993, with bin Laden personally involved.
Bin Laden and al-Qa'ida clearly seek chemical, biological and nuclear weapons, an interest dating back to at least 1993.
The group likely lacks the technical skill to make high-end chemical, biological or nuclear weapons, and has fallen for nuclear scams.
Low-end chemical and biological agents such as cholera could eventually be within reach.
The greatest threat is bin Laden acting as acquisition agent for a state sponsor such as Iraq.
Instability in Pakistan, if fundamentalists seized nuclear assets, could give bin Laden a role advocating nuclear use.
Vehicle bombs are likely to remain al-Qa'ida's dominant tool for some time.
The author considers a radiological dispersion device the most probable route to a successful WMD attack by bin Laden and his associates.
Chem/bio purchase or theft is described as the easiest route, and the text says bin Laden's associates have already tried it.
Bin Laden is judged to have ample funding for most low-end chemical, biological and radiological options.
Nuclear weapon manufacture or purchase/theft is rated far less probable because of technical difficulty, cost and security.
State sponsorship cannot be ruled out as a source of help in acquiring and employing WMD.
Low-end chem/bio agents such as phosgene are comparatively easy to obtain and use, so the threat should not be dismissed even if high-end agents are hard to make.
State sponsorship or theft may supply WMD agents to terrorists, making manufacturing difficulty an unreliable gauge of risk.
Al-Qaeda should be relatively easy to penetrate because it actively recruits, has large numbers, screens recruits cursorily, and trains fighters for many causes.
Targeting bin Laden directly is the most controversial option; he may be easily replaced by someone more reckless, or become a martyr.
Bin Laden's strength is channeling existing ethnic and religious discontent against the US, so addressing that discontent matters more than addressing bin Laden alone.
US policy toward the Taliban and Pakistan is seen as discriminatory in the Islamic world, and the US failed to justify the 1998 strikes diplomatically.
Bin Laden is revered as a war hero by many Afghans, so the Taliban find it politically difficult to hand him over openly.
The authors argue covert options (secret expulsion, tip-offs, snatch) are more feasible for the Taliban than overt ones.
The authors contend that bin Laden's strength lies in tapping widespread Muslim discontent rather than in his personal organizational skills.
The authors recommend depersonalizing the conflict by focusing on al Qaeda rather than bin Laden's name and limiting his media access.
Bin Laden moved from Sudan to Afghanistan in 1996 after Sudan expelled him.
Bin Laden financed and organized Arab volunteers in the 1980s Afghan war through the MAK, guesthouses, and camps, co-founded with Abdullah Azzam.
Bin Laden was most closely allied with Gulbuddin Hekmatyar's Islamic Party among Afghan factions.
Al-Qa'ida was reportedly named around 1988 as the bin Laden complex tracking volunteers; the document also conflates it with the Islamic Salvation Foundation.
Egyptian Islamic Jihad under Zawahiri and the Islamic Group are closely tied to bin Laden and allied with al-Qa'ida, though the Islamic Group reportedly cut ties in July 1998.
Bin Laden is suspected of financing the 1995 Mubarak assassination attempt and the 1997 Luxor attack, the latter through Mustafa Hamza.
Pakistan hosted bin Laden-linked guesthouses and Arab Afghan bases (Su Casa house, Pabi camp), and Pakistani militant groups such as Harkat Ansar and LeT were seen as his human assets.
A Pakistani security official said groups like Harkat Ansar give bin Laden a formidable human asset in Pakistan.
Bin Laden reportedly funded Abu Sayyaf and MILF, though MILF leaders say they cut off his aid in 1998.
Saudi Arabia progressively moved against bin Laden from 1991 to 1994, ending in loss of citizenship.
Bin Laden is linked to the 1995 Riyadh and 1996 Khobar bombings via communiqués, praise and alleged claims.
Saudi intelligence chief Turki al-Faisal claims Mullah Omar agreed in June 1998 to surrender bin Laden, which the Taliban deny.
Bin Laden is alleged to have ties to Iran and Hezbollah, including training and Tehran meetings in 1996-97.
Bangladeshi security officials and arrested suspects claim bin Laden financed Harkat-ul-Jihad, including reportedly $1 million via four Dhaka accounts, to bring Taliban-style rule to Bangladesh.
Harkat-ul-Jihad in Bangladesh was formed by 1995 at a Chittagong seminary and sent trained recruits to fight alongside the Taliban.
Intelligence reports allege bin Laden met Iranian intelligence and Hezbollah figures in Tehran in 1996-97 to coordinate terrorism.
Bin Laden is alleged to have supported or trained militants from Eritrea, Ethiopia, Tajikistan, Chechnya, Kosovo and the Philippines (via Malaysia).
Chechen commander Khattab, a veteran of the Afghan jihad, is linked by intelligence reports to bin Laden; Pakistani mujahideen under Safir Ahmed, who met bin Laden in Jalalabad, assisted him.
Zawahri's Egyptian Jihad is said to give material backing to Chechen rebels and to run networks in Azerbaijan, UK and Austria.
Khalid al-Fawwaz in London is alleged to be bin Laden's UK representative and al Qaeda UK head, with seized documents showing fax contacts in ten US cities.
The 1998 US indictment alleges an al Qaeda-Iraq understanding on non-hostility and cooperation in weapons development.
Harakat-ul-Ansar/Harakat ul-Mujahideen trained in bin Laden's camps and received the Khost camps from the Taliban in 1996.
Bin Laden moved to Afghanistan in May 1996 under the area of Yunis Khalis, then to Kandahar by 1997.
Indian police linked the Nasir plot against US missions in India to bin Laden.
Bin Laden financed the Taliban and built a house for Mullah Omar, but senior Taliban like Hassan and Rabbani resented him.
The Taliban prevented a Pakistani commando attempt on bin Laden in April 1997.
Uganda foiled a 1998 Kampala embassy bomb plot by suspects trained in Sudan with bin Laden ties.
Bin Laden and Zawahiri were the leading figures of the International Islamic Front formed Feb 1998, uniting Egyptian groups with Pakistani and Bangladeshi movements.
The Taliban protected bin Laden, disarming Pakistani commandos in 1997 and refusing US requests to surrender him in 1998, though Mullah Omar reportedly reprimanded him after his press conference.
Saudi intelligence obtained defectors from bin Laden's finance apparatus, including treasurer Mohamed bin Moisalih, who disclosed banking channels.
Bin Laden's East African cell, led by Wadih El Hage with Haroun Fazil as deputy, was identified by the CIA by Aug 1997 and disrupted by the raid on El Hage's home.
Abu Ubaidah al Banshiri set up Odeh's Mombasa fish business as cover for surveillance of the US embassy in Nairobi.
Egyptian Jihad built networks in Albania under humanitarian cover; 1998 US-assisted rendition of members may have provoked the embassy bombings.
Warnings about Nairobi embassy plots in 1997 (Al Haramain informant, Mustafa Mahmoud Said Ahmed) were judged unreliable.
Fazul Abdullah Mohammed rented the Nairobi villa, chaired the 2 Aug 1998 Hilltop Hotel meeting, and led the bomb convoy.
Planning for the bombings was directed by Egyptian Islamic Jihad member Ali Saleh, per Odeh's confession, indicating EIJ–al Qaeda operational integration.
The June 1998 deportation of EIJ members from Albania to Egypt is suggested as a possible trigger for the attacks.
Prince Turki says Mullah Omar agreed in June 1998 to surrender bin Laden, but the Taliban deny any such agreement.
Bin Laden used Said Sayyed Salameh to finance fundamentalist factions in Libya and Egypt through African channels.
The Nairobi bombing was carried out by an al-Qaida Kenya cell led by Fazul with Odeh as explosives consultant and al-Owhali as truck passenger.
Odeh claimed the embassy attacks were sponsored by bin Laden.
Odeh trained in Afghan al-Qaida camps and was sent to Somalia by Saiful Adil, linking al-Qaida to anti-UN fighters in Somalia.
Al-Owhali met bin Laden around 1996 and asked for a mission.
Wadih el Hage was linked to Fazul and the Kenya cell and attended Odeh's wedding.
The bomb explosives were reportedly sourced from Luanda and smuggled into Kenya gradually.
The RARB found the embassies had no warning intelligence and inadequate vehicle-bomb setback and preparation.
Wadih el Hage, a US citizen, served as bin Laden's secretary in Sudan and led the Kenya al Qaeda cell, using a US passport and charity fronts.
Ali Mohamed, a former US Army sergeant, trained militants in New York and al Qaeda members, and moved bin Laden to Sudan in 1991 and back to Afghanistan in 1996.
Ali Mohamed was in contact with the FBI from 1993 and conducted surveillance of the US Embassy in Nairobi in 1994.
The Al Kifah Refugee Center in Brooklyn linked Afghan jihad recruitment to people later convicted in the WTC and Landmarks cases.
